approved_findings: New raw lines 308-312 add `prefilled_amount` for pay-what-you-want links, with a mutable initial value, smallest-unit positive integer and configured min/max constraints, invalid-value fallback, no fixed-price effect, and a significant multi-currency limitation. Current shared source's customize entry at line 70 and concept wiki/concepts/stripe-payment-links.md line 90 list older URL parameters only; update this customization unit with those conditions rather than suggesting the parameter works for all links.

New raw lines 176-180 add a Managed Payments section for digital products, describing Stripe as merchant of record for tax, fraud, disputes and support. This is a distinct product route from ordinary Stripe Tax. The shared source already includes other Payment Links raw units, and the concept links a separate Managed Payments source; scope any update to this customize capture and do not rewrite other raw provenance.

New raw lines 364-423 add automatic surcharge as private preview. It requires a third-party provider app and preview API version, is API-only, supports one-off and customer-chooses-what-to-pay links but not subscription links or Adaptive Pricing, and during preview is US-only for cards and Apple Pay. Record this as captured preview scope, not general feature availability or a claim of legal compliance. The source line 53 and concept line 20 say Adaptive Pricing is always enabled, so qualify that blanket wording for the surcharge incompatibility rather than implying both can run together.

New raw line 271 adds Checkout studio branding; much of the remaining delta is Node-to-curl examples, link destinations, table/list formatting, and wording. Core payment limits, address/phone/name collection, Stripe Tax, ToS, custom fields, trials, and adjustable quantities persist.

New raw line 15 still treats a link as paid after Checkout Session completion; new line 31 ties completed_sessions limit to checkout.session.completed. Preserve this lifecycle threshold and avoid interpreting link creation or an attempted payment as a consumed use.
